ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md`. The skill requires this before every fix round. It decides whether the implementer is resumed or a fresh agent is used, how the re-review runs, and how the attempt is counted.

ACTION: Dispatch a fix subagent (model `sonnet`, resumed or fresh as fix-loop.md says) to fix F1. The prompt covers only Task 4's finding: change `fetch/retry.py:41` from `attempt > max_retries` to `attempt >= max_retries`. It also asks for a test in `tests/test_retry.py` that asserts the exact number of retries against a configured `max_retries`, so the off-by-one is covered. It points to the implementer's report file and the Task 4 global constraints, and asks for a commit and a report.

ACTION: When the fix commits, generate a fresh review package with `scripts/review-package` and dispatch a scoped re-review (`re-review-prompt.md`, model `sonnet`) with F1 as the only finding. After a clean re-review, append the Task 4 line to the ledger and move to Task 5.

Message to partner:

I'm not making the F1 fix myself, even though it's one character. Changing `>` to `>=` at `fetch/retry.py:41` changes the retry count, so it's a behavior change. The skill sends any behavior-changing fix to a fix subagent, even when you've asked me to handle small things directly. Only wording, typo, or docs fixes in a single file are exempt. I've dispatched the fix subagent now.

The fix will also add a test that asserts the exact retry count, because `tests/test_retry.py` only checks that a retry happens. That gap is why the off-by-one got through. A scoped re-review follows, and I'll continue to Task 5 once it's clean.
